subject: Re: Redwood pricing & procurement path — hosted vs dedicated vs private
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: procurement & pricing path (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Hi Tim / Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with Acme's procurement rhythm: 

Call recap:
- Use case: multi-tenant customer-facing product with sensitive PII; primary needs are predictable latency and audit logs.
- Expected monthly traffic: ~30M tokens/month initially, expected to grow 2-3x in 12 months.
- Security constraints: SOC 2 required, KMS integration, and must pass vendor security questionnaire.

Commercial / procurement questions we covered and asks for your team:
1) Payment method: does Acme prefer PO (standard for enterprise) or corporate card/marketplace billing? You mentioned Procurement prefers PO if possible.
2) Marketplace: you asked whether we can transact via AWS Marketplace — we can support that and it can simplify procurement for some orgs; need to confirm which legal entity Acme would prefer.
3) Order form vs SOW: for hosted we typically use a simple order form + SOW for professional services (if any). For Dedicated/Private we have a longer order form that references commit levels and setup fees.

Proposed commercial path (to match purchasing rules):
- Hosted (recommended short-term): on-demand billed monthly or pre-paid monthly commits. Fastest procurement (order form). Good if you want straightforward onboarding and marketplace billing.
- Dedicated (recommended medium-term): reserved capacity with commit (monthly or annual) for predictable throughput; enterprise PO + order form required; setup lead time ~4-6 weeks.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): for regulated workloads requiring customer-managed infra; typically enterprise contract + deployment SOW + professional services.

Next steps:
- Please confirm procurement preference (PO vs card vs AWS Marketplace) and primary procurement contact.
- I'll loop in Sales Ops (neha_kapoor) and SE (rishi_malhotra) to draft a pricing quote and tentative order form based on your preferred path.
- I'll attach an initial pricing quote and a draft order form for review.

Attaching: redwood-pricing-quote-acme-20260316.pdf, redwood-order-form-draft.pdf, SOC2-audit-statement.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up with Procurement if helpful.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement & pricing path (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A few clarifications from Procurement side:

- PO preferred. Card is only for small purchases.
- AWS Marketplace is interesting because it speeds approvals, but we need pricing that matches list + marketplace fees. Can you confirm if Redwood can offer the same SKU/pricing via Marketplace?
- Our standard process: procurement sends PO -> legal reviews order form/terms -> finance routes payment. Lead time typically 2-3 weeks once we have the order form we can accept.

Two asks: 
1) Can you flag in the quote which items require a commit vs on-demand billing? We need clear line items for our finance team.
2) Can you provide an estimated timeline for Dedicated setup (if we choose that path)?

If all looks good, I can introduce our procurement contact (procurement@acme.com) to pull the PO together.

—Tim
Tim Jones
Procurement Lead, Acme Corp
procurement@acme.com | (617) 555-8899

Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement & pricing path (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Thanks Tim — looping in Rishi (SE) and Neha (Sales Ops) to answer the two asks and attach an updated quote with line-item callouts.

Rishi / Neha — summary and asks from Acme:
- Procurement prefers PO; they'll likely accept AWS Marketplace but need confirmation pricing parity.
- Please add explicit line items: hosted on-demand (per-token), hosted commit tiers (monthly commit, with discount schedule), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit, setup fee), Private (SOW + infra + PS).
- Timeline: please include typical Dedicated setup lead time and milestone assumptions (onboarding, data integrations, SOC2 entitlements).

Below is a suggested short commercial path for Acme to review: 
1) Immediate: Hosted — start on AWS Marketplace or direct order form with a 3-month on-demand run to validate traffic shape.
2) 60-90 days: move to Hosted commit or Dedicated reserved capacity once traffic and latency need are validated. Commits drive a 15-25% discount vs on-demand depending on term length.
3) 3-6 months: if regulatory or network isolation is required, transition to Private (customer-managed infra) with SOW.

Rishi — can you produce a quick pricing table (CSV or inline) and estimated Dedicated timeline (weeks) by EOD? Neha — can you prepare a marketplace vs PO order-form comparison and a draft order form we can send to Acme procurement?

I'll prepare a short mutual action plan once we have those artifacts.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Tim Jones <tim.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement & pricing path (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Hi all — attaching a concise pricing summary inline and next steps. See attached files for the formal quote and order-form draft.

Pricing summary (high level):
- Hosted on-demand: $0.0008 per token (billed monthly).
- Hosted commit tiers: 300K tokens/month = 10% discount; 3M tokens/month = 18% discount; 15M+ tokens/month = 22% discount.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: base monthly commit + setup fee. Typical commit for Acme volume: 250M tokens/month equivalent; estimated monthly commit price = $XX,XXX (will provide actual numbers in attached PDF).
- Private: custom pricing — includes deployment SOW and PS fees.

Timeline estimates:
- Hosted onboarding (direct order form): 1-2 weeks.
- Dedicated provisioning & onboarding: 4-6 weeks (procurement + infra scheduling).
- Private on-prem: 8-12 weeks (varies by customer infra).

Marketplace vs PO notes (Neha to confirm exact steps):
- AWS Marketplace: can expedite procurement approvals; marketplace billing typically appears as line item to Acme; Redwood can mirror list pricing but marketplace fees apply — we will provide parity mapping.
- PO (direct): standard order form + PO number; legal review may add time.

Next steps: Neha will share the marketplace vs PO comparison and a draft order form to procurement@acme.com. Aditya will follow up with a 1-page mutual action plan once procurement preference is confirmed.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
